Instead of concluding anything, she went to each in turn and said, "That was a lot to hear. How are you doing with it?" The first colleague said they were worried about their contract. The second said they were relieved that their project was safe. Sarita listened to each without promising anything. She told me later that she had guessed wrong about the second, taking the sigh for gloom. I have asked her to share what she learned about checking in with the team leads.

passage: Thursday, 9 pm. Vidya's log. Today the manager announced that the client had approved our proposal. Raghav's eyes went wide, then he exhaled loudly and put his head in his hands for a second. My first thought was, he's disappointed? Then his voice came out tight: "Well. That's great." I nearly walked away. Instead, at the tea machine I said, "You looked hit by that news. Everything okay?" He laughed. "I'm so relieved I can't think. I've been afraid we'd lose the project since March." I'd have got it completely wrong. He is also a bit worried, he said, because now we have to deliver by June. Note to self: cues tell me something's up, not what. Asking took ten seconds, and he said thanks. 🙂

qa.a: He said he was so relieved he could not think, and that he had been afraid they would lose the project since March.

passage: At the block office in Chhindwara district, the notice came by email at noon: the new primary health centre for Lalit's village had finally been approved. Disha watched Lalit read it. His eyes went wide, he let out a long breath, and when he spoke, his voice was tight and strange. "It's approved." Then he went out onto the verandah and stood very still with his back to everyone. Disha couldn't read it. Was he worried about the land it would take? Upset about something she didn't know? She gave him a few minutes, then went out with two cups of tea and stood beside him. "You looked surprised in there. Are you okay?" He took the tea, eyes wet. "Relieved. My mother had to travel forty kilometres for every check-up last year. Now the village won't have to." Disha nodded and said nothing more, letting him have the quiet. After a while he laughed shakily. "Don't tell anyone I cried at a notice."

qa.q: How far did Lalit's mother have to travel for check-ups?
qa.a: Forty kilometres.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling after reading the notice?
qa.a: Lalit felt surprised and deeply relieved, even tearful, because his mother and village would no longer travel so far for care.

qa.q: How did Disha check in well?
qa.a: She gave him a few minutes, joined him with tea, named what she saw and asked if he was okay, then let him have quiet.

qa.q: What would have changed if Disha had assumed Lalit was upset about the land?
qa.a: She might have offered the wrong comfort or asked awkward questions, missing that he was actually relieved.

grounding: Shows a young professional reading a colleague's widened eyes, sigh and tight voice at news, and a calm check-in revealing relief.

passage: When the email came through that their grant had been approved, the whole lab in São Paulo cheered. Yara smiled too, but Beatriz noticed that her voice when she said "Great news" was tight and high, and her hands were gripping her coffee cup. Beatriz couldn't tell what was underneath. Nerves about leading it? Something at home? Later, when the others had gone to lunch, Beatriz sat down beside her. "You seemed a bit tense when the grant came in. I might be reading it wrong. How are you feeling about it?" Yara let out a breath. "Happy. And terrified. It means four months of fieldwork in Manaus, and my father's been unwell. I don't know how to tell my mother." Beatriz nodded. "That's a lot at once. Do you want to talk it through, or just sit for a bit?" "Talk. Please." They skipped lunch.

qa.q: How long will Yara's fieldwork in Manaus last?
qa.a: Four months.

qa.q: What was Yara feeling about the grant?
qa.a: Yara felt happy and terrified at once, worried about leaving for fieldwork while her father was unwell.

qa.q: What made Beatriz's check-in careful?
qa.a: She waited for a private moment, described the tense cue while admitting she might be wrong, asked how Yara felt, then offered talk or quiet.

qa.q: How did the rest of the lab react to the grant?
qa.a: The rest of the lab cheered, reading only good news, unaware of Yara's mixed feelings.

grounding: Shows a young professional noticing a colleague's tense voice at good news and a calm check-in revealing worry alongside joy.

subtype: Surprised, relieved and worried at work [Interpreting]
passage: At 10:15 the whole floor of the Gangtok insurance office went quiet as the email landed: the claims unit would shrink by four posts, and the rural outreach pilot was approved. Dolma glanced across at Ganga. Ganga's eyes went wide, then she let out a long sigh and pressed her palms flat on the desk. When the supervisor passed, Ganga said, "All good, all good," in a voice pulled tight as wire. Dolma's mind ran ahead: was Ganga's post one of the four? Or was that sigh relief, since the pilot was Ganga's idea? She didn't ask in front of everyone. At the tea break she waited until they were alone by the window. "That email was a lot. How are you taking it?" Ganga laughed shakily. "Both ways. My pilot got through, and I'm thrilled. But my cousin is in claims, and I've no idea if she's safe." Dolma nodded and passed her the biscuit tin.

qa.q: How many posts would the claims unit lose?
qa.a: The claims unit would shrink by four posts.

qa.q: What did Ganga's wide eyes and long sigh most likely show, and what else could they have meant?
qa.a: They showed surprise and mixed feelings: Ganga was thrilled about the pilot yet worried for her cousin in claims; before asking, Dolma could just as easily have read them as fear for Ganga's own post.

qa.q: What made Dolma's check-in work?
qa.a: Dolma waited for a private moment and asked an open, calm question instead of guessing, so Ganga could explain both feelings 🙏

qa.q: How might the supervisor have read Ganga's "All good, all good"?
qa.a: The supervisor may have taken the words at face value and believed Ganga was fine, missing the worry in the tight voice.

grounding: Shows a young professional reading a colleague's wide eyes, sigh and tense voice at mixed news, and using a calm check-in to learn the cause.
